column1: # box_cell_shapes.tsv -- THE CELL-SHAPE TABLE: the words each box kind carves on the spine at its alpha (ARCH-ZETA-ONE-COORDINATE 3.5 (iii);
# ARCH-THREE-ZETAS-EMISSION 2 (ZALPHA) and 10 (3); the cto, CEO-1923). The planner's carve K_i is this row's alpha_words plus 16 x the spine
# locals first used at the box plus a disjunction's arm extra. util_gen_box_cell_shapes.py writes SCRIP/src/planner/box_cell_shapes.inc from this
# file (--write) and refuses a stale one (--check); the planner's zd_k_own reads the generated rows. Started from zd_k_own (zeta_plan.cpp) as it
# stood at SCRIP c22b86a9b, row for row, so the first landing is byte-identical; a switch moves a kind's state into its own carve by editing its row.
# ROWS ARE EVALUATED TOP TO BOTTOM AND THE FIRST MATCH WINS. THE CONDITIONS OF ONE KIND'S ROWS ARE DISJOINT ACROSS REGIMES (the cfo, 2026-10-24, on the
# ceo's 7ed02df91 finding: the Icon switch's IR_BOUND 16 home_frame row sat ahead of D3's IR_BOUND 0 pl_home and stole 23 Prolog core entries, because home_frame
# and home_state were true of a Prolog home-frame graph too): a condition that names a regime (icn_*, pl_*) is true of that regime's graphs ONLY -- BCS_ICN_HOME is
# false for a Prolog resumable callable (08efb562e, 8e3edbe62), BCS_PL_HOME false for an Icon graph -- so no row of one regime can match another regime's node
# whatever the order; a generic condition (home_frame, home_state, has_operands, always) comes AFTER every regime row of the same kind, and row order carries no
# other meaning. A new row for a kind another regime also carves names its regime in its condition or goes below that regime's rows; util_gen_box_cell_shapes.py
# --check regenerates the .inc and a reviewer reads the kind's rows together. Columns:
#   kind          the IR kind (IR_*), or * for any kind

#   alpha_words   the bytes the box carves at its alpha, or arm_spine (the disjunction's computed arm extent, zd_dj_spine), or call_args (16 x (2 + the call's argument count), or call_argv (16 x (1 + the argument count)) or call_argv_cur (16 x (2 + the argument count)), or fence_spine (planner_fence_k: 16 for a bounded body, 0 for a frame-homed record), or alt_spine (planner_alt_k: 32 plus the largest arm's live cells, 48 when an arm is unbounded)

#   when          always | call_curmov (a call that moves the cursor) | call_argv (one of the eleven call kinds of bb_call_fn.cpp: direct, pl_leaf, pas_bi, callee_rec, field_rec, byname, try, method, redisp, apply, eval) | call_argv_cur (call_argv and the call moves the cursor) | icn_local (an Icon local variable read in a spine-cells graph) |

#                 icn_suspend (an Icon suspend in a spine-cells graph) | icn_home (a home-frame graph that is not Prolog-resumable: Icon, and Raku and Pascal where a row names their kinds) | has_operands | no_operands | patv (a static PATV$ deferred pattern)
#   word_kind     the kind of every 8-byte word of the carve, in ascending address (ARCH-GC-COMPILE-TIME-FRAME-MAPS 16, the cto 2026-10-29, CEO-2011): a string over D (one 16-byte
#                 DESCR cell, whose FIRST word is the one the collector's spine walk visits) and r (one raw 8-byte word: TO's counter and limit, LIMIT's count and flag, a scan's
#                 saved cursor, a choice header); [D] or [r] once marks the computed middle (call_args: the argument cells; alt_spine, fence_spine: raw); '-' for a carve of 0.
#                 A numeric alpha_words and arm_spine (32) and arm_spine_hdr (64) are checked against the string's width by util_gen_box_cell_shapes.py. A node's sticky locals
#                 (16 bytes each, DT_SNUL at alpha) are D cells right after this part, then the disjunction arm extra (raw until an arm writes it).
#   gamma_release, omega_release, fenced    the gamma law's columns, '-' until pass (iv) reads them from here
#   source        why the box carves what it carves

D3 kind 7 (the cfo's ruling of 2026-10-24 16:15): an if-then-else or negation BOUND (its omega is the GATE, a fence UNMARK commits it) whose CONDITION span carries no excursion, or a BOUND the home pass proves sits in a definite run (planner_bound_spine), carves its record on the spine -- mark +0, saved rsp +8, banked B +16, the choice header to +40 -- read by its UNMARKs through the planner's cross-cell distance or the rbp alias; the arm-failure road reads nothing of it after the fence

the bound's record (mark +0, rsp at entry +8, banked B +16, boundary +32) outlives the commit's whack-pop and is read by the fence's omega UNMARK and the gate at the construct's base depth: no fixed rsp distance reaches it, so it is resident in the activation frame (Lon's TEST 2; D3 batch 2)

a call box that moves the cursor (flat cell rule, ARCH-ZETA-LAYOUT R1, step 2a): the result at +0, the cursor save at +16 and the argument block at +32, one DESCR per operand; the call's own argument copy is a cell word, never a second carve

a call box (flat cell rule, ARCH-ZETA-LAYOUT R1, step 2a): the result at +0 and the argument block at +16, one DESCR per operand; the argument copy the callee reads is a cell word, never a second carve

the local's own cell is its home; the read carves nothing
the suspend passes its value up; its resume is the beta

the bound read across a retaining edge keeps its record in the activation frame (Lon's TEST 2)

a call whose callee may retain, through the block protocol (planner_call_spine_record): the result, then the resume record at +16 -- {DT_RAW | the callee's beta << 8, the callee's rbp}, null at alpha, written over by the landing that pushes a fresh 32-byte cell below a retained frame -- read back at beta at a fixed rsp distance; no act word in the activation frame (ARCH-PROLOG-ACTIVATION-LIFETIME 8.1)
a call that may retain its callee's frame: the result cell, with the act word resident in the activation frame (Lon's TEST 2) (D3)
a definite call: the result beside the act word (+16, +24), read back at beta at a fixed rsp distance (D3)

call/N on a home-set Prolog graph (planner_call_spine_record): the result, then the resume record at +16 -- {DT_RAW | the callee's beta << 8, the callee's rbp}, null at alpha, written over by the landing that pushes a fresh 32-byte cell below a retained frame -- read back at beta at a fixed rsp distance; the goal and its extra arguments are read from their own cells, no staging and no act word in the activation frame (ARCH-PROLOG-ACTIVATION-LIFETIME 8.1)
call/N never knows its callee (PR_UNKNOWN_CALLEE): the result cell, with the argument block and the act word resident (D3)

the live-arm index (+16) is written by GATE_ARM at each arm's depth and read at the gate's beta at the construct's base, across the arms' pops: no fixed rsp distance reaches it, so it is resident in the activation frame (Lon's TEST 2; D3 batch 2)
the bound's record is a frame word today (chunk 2, the switches)
its value is its last operand's

the end of an if-then-else arm on a home-set Prolog graph pushes its live-arm index {DT_RAW, arm} as its own spine cell, below the join wall, so the GATE's beta -- entered when the continuation popped back to the construct's exit depth -- reads it at [rsp + 8] and pops it with the arm's pair distance; no gate word in the activation frame (ARCH-PROLOG-ACTIVATION-LIFETIME 8.2)

the setup_call_cleanup record (state, link, banked B at +16..+40) is ACT by construction: its goal is the retaining edge, so on a home-set Prolog graph the record is resident in the activation frame and carves nothing on the spine (D3 kind 3)
the result leaves through the return block
